answer: Rhythm-gated admission. Each new identity must submit its first N messages on a schedule drawn from a shared timing vine: intervals cluster near a common vertex, and deviations past a fixed threshold flag the account. A node reaching the summit of normal traffic shape earns standing; sybils can't fake that curve cheaply. An attacker pays per-identity with sustained, correctly paced traffic—real compute and latency—so mass registration becomes slow and expensive, not just costly in fees.
